body.p: Claims 1-26 were previously pending with Claims 1, 12, and 23 being independent. Claims 1, 12, and 23 have been amended herein. Support for the amendments can be found at the least at

Claims 1-5, 7, 12-16, and 23-25 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly obvious over U.S. Patent Publication No. 2006/0247508 to Fennell (hereinafter "Fennell") in view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0245910 to Mallas et al. (hereinafter "Mallas") in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2019/0167,167 to Mitchell (hereinafter "Mitchell") and in further view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2020/0338351 to Panken (hereinafter "Panken"). Claims 6 and 17 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 allegedly obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell in view of Panken and in further view of U.S. Patent Publication No. 2002/0042561 to Schulman et al. ("Schulman"). Claims 8-11, 19-22, and 26 stand rejected as allegedly being obvious over Fennell in view of Mallas in view of Mitchell in view of Panken and in further view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0270,617 to Muller ("Muller"). As a prima facie case of the obviousness of claims 1-26 cannot be established based upon the asserted combination of references, Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections as set forth below.

Applicant submits that Panken is non-analogous art. Art is analogous when it is: (1) from the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention; or (2) reasonably pertinent to the particular problem faced by the inventor, if the art is not from the same field of endeavor. In re Bigio, 381 F.3d 1320, 1325-1326 (Fed. Cir. 2004); In re Wood and Eversole, 599 F.2d 1032, 1036 (CCPA 1979).

1. Here, the field of endeavor is analyte monitoring in interstitial fluid. Panken's field of endeavor is determining source locations of electrical signals in a brain by providing hypothetical locations and comparing the hypothetical locations to measured signals. Applicant respectfully submits that the skilled person would not find that a field directed to determining source locations of electrical signals in the brain as in any way related to analyte monitoring in interstitial fluid. It
is the Office's burden to identify analogous art, and here, the Office has not show how Panken is in the same field of endeavor to the claimed invention.

2. In order to be "reasonably pertinent," art must "logically commend itself' to an inventor's attention in considering his problem. In re Icon Health and Fitness, Inc., 496 F.3d 1374, 1379-80 (Fed. Cir. 2007)(citing In re Clay, 966 F.2d 656, 658-59 (Fed. Cir. 1992)). See also MPEP § 2141.01(a). The current application solves the problem of slow reaction time in glucose monitoring. Specifically, "[b]y providing real-time glucose concentrations, therapeutic/clinical actions may be applied more timely and the glycemic condition may be better controlled." Specification, [0003].

Furthermore, the Federal Circuit has confirmed that a reference qualifies as prior art only when it is analogous to the claimed invention. See In re Klein, 647F.3d 1343 (Fed. Cir. 2011); Innovention Toys, LLC, No. 2010-1290, slip op. at 12. "[T]his court has previously 'reminded ... the PTO that it is necessary to consider 'the reality of the circumstances' - in other words, common sense - in deciding in which fields a person of ordinary skill would reasonably be expected to look for a solution to the problem facing the inventor." Id. at 1326 (quoting In re Oetiker, 977 F.2d 1443, 1447 (Fed. Cir. 1992) (quoting In re Wood, 599 F.2d 1032, 1036 (CCPA 1979)).

Applicant submits that a PHOSITA considering "the reality of the circumstances" and using "common sense" would not find brain wave detection to be an obvious field to find solutions for problems arising in the field of blood glucose monitoring. As such, Applicant submits that Panken does not meet the requirements for analogous art and should be removed as a reference.

The Office Action references Panken at [0082] to allegedly teach, in combination with Fennell, Mallas, and Mitchell, the claimed working electrode voltage source, counter electrode voltage source, and guard ring voltage source. Applicant submits that a boilerplate statement such as "stimulation generation circuitry 202 may comprise multiple voltage or current sources and sinks that are coupled to respective electrodes to drive the electrodes as cathodes or anodes" (Panken, [0082]) does not meet the MPEP requirements for rejecting the claims under 35 U.S.C. § 103. The instant claim limitations require "a working electrode voltage source," "a counter electrode voltage source," and "a guard ring voltage source" that are "separate and distinct voltage sources." Support for these limitations can be found at the least at [0040]-[0044] of the

Specification. Furthermore, these separate and distinct voltage sources are illustrated in FIG. 5. The claims require a particular system comprising specific components that are not included in any combination of the currently cited art. The instant claims have been amended to clarify the distinctions with the cited art. Applicant submits that generally referencing boiler-plate material from (non-analogous) art that generally states that a power source may be multiple power sources does not teach the specifically claimed hardware components and the specific arrangement of those hardware components as claimed. Applicant submits that the current rejections are therefore deficient and respectfully requests a Notice of Allowance or a new Non-Final Office Action that corrects the above-stated deficiencies.

Applicant respectfully submits that those dependent claims not discussed separately herein are allowable at least for the reasons discussed with respect to the corresponding independent claims, and respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 103 rejections thereof be withdrawn.

Applicant submits that claims 1-26, as amended, are in allowable condition and request a corresponding Notice of Allowance. In the event of any outstanding issues, Applicants respectfully request an Examiner Interview to expedite prosecution. Any additional fee that might be due in connection with this application should be applied against Deposit Account No. 50-6159.
